security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU executes vghsh.vs or vgmul.vs without checking that the vd register group overlaps the vs2 scalar element group. In the .vs form, vs2 holds a single 128-bit scalar element group (the hash subkey H or multiplicand) broadcast across all element groups of vd. If vd overlaps vs2, the in-place read-modify-write of vd corrupts the scalar key material before it is applied to all element groups, producing incorrect GHASH results.
security_spec.summary: Zvkgs adds .vs variants of vghsh/vgmul where vs2 is a scalar element group broadcast to all vd element groups; QEMU must enforce the vd/vs2 non-overlap constraint or the scalar key is corrupted during in-place updates

findings.finding: QEMU only implements vgmul.vv (the .vv form from Zvkg). The Zvkgs extension, which adds vgmul.vs (the .vs scalar element group form), is not implemented. No vgmul.vs encoding exists in insn32.decode, no trans_vgmul_vs function exists, no ext_zvkgs config flag exists, and no HELPER(vgmul_vs) exists. The vgmul.vv form reads vs2 per-element-group (vs2[i*2+0], vs2[i*2+1]) and does not require the .vs-specific vd-vs2 overlap check. The spec itself notes at zvk.adoc:2752-2757 that .vs variants are described as a 'future extension'. Since the .vs instructions do not exist in QEMU, the vulnerability described in the security spec (vd overlapping vs2 scalar element group in .vs form) cannot occur.

spec_citations.excerpt: [#norm:veccrypto_vsins_vs2]#In the case of the `.vs` instructions defined in this specification, `vs2` holds a 128-bit scalar element group.# [#norm:veccrypto_vsins_vdvs2overlap]#For implementations with `VLEN` ≥ 128, `vs2` refers to a single register. Thus, the `vd` register group must not overlap the `vs2` register. However, in implementations where `VLEN` < 128, `vs2` refers to a register group comprised of the number of registers needed to hold the 128-bit scalar element group. In this case, the `vd` register group must not overlap this `vs2` register group.#

Since the same hash subkey `H` will typically be used repeatedly on a given message, a future extension might define a vector-scalar version of this instruction where `vs2` is the scalar element group. This would help reduce register pressure when `LMUL` > 1.

findings.finding: QEMU only implements vghsh.vv (the .vv form from Zvkg). The Zvkgs extension, which adds vghsh.vs (the .vs scalar element group form), is not implemented. No vghsh.vs encoding exists in insn32.decode, no trans_vghsh_vs function exists, no HELPER(vghsh_vs) exists. The vghsh.vv form reads vs2 per-element-group (vs2[i*2+0], vs2[i*2+1] at vcrypto_helper.c:808) and writes vd per-element-group (vd[i*2+0], vd[i*2+1] at vcrypto_helper.c:827). In the .vv form, vs2 is a full vector register group consumed in lockstep with vd, so the .vs-specific scalar-overlap concern does not apply. The spec explicitly describes .vs as a future extension at zvk.adoc:2633-2636.

findings.finding: This helper implements the .vv form correctly: it reads vs2 per-element-group at line 808 (vs2[i*2+0], vs2[i*2+1]), so each 128-bit element group gets its own copy of the hash subkey H. The .vs form (Zvkgs) would require a different helper that reads vs2 only once at indices [0] and [1] and broadcasts that single scalar element group across all vd element groups. No such HELPER(vghsh_vs) exists. The existing HELPER(vghsh_vv) correctly implements the Zvkg .vv specification (zvk.adoc:2638-2675).
